messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] severity=P1 GPU pool 'prod-gpu-a' limited capacity - queue growth observed > 95th pct, autoscaler not triggering. Paging oncall.

sara (oncall): got the page, I'm on it. starting timeline & impact assessment.

ben (eng-sre): seeing sustained enqueued jobs on the inference-queue cluster, backlog went from ~120 -> ~800 in 7m. pods at 100% GPU utilization. HPA target pod count stuck at 12/12.

priya (runtime): metrics we're feeding the HPA (custom/gpu_queue_depth) show zeros for the last 6m from prometheus-adapter in cluster-a. Prometheus itself has scrape success dropping to 60% for node-exporter and metrics-server errors.

mike (infra): can confirm control-plane didn't try to scale. kube-controller logs show repeated 504 from prometheus-adapter: `http2: server sent GOAWAY` and a raft of timeouts in the adapter pod.

sara (oncall): hypothesis: adapter/backfill pipeline lag -> HPA sees stale/zero metrics -> no scale. Is there any recent deploys to adapter or network change?

priya (runtime): Deploys: adapter had a non-prod canary rolled yesterday, but prod adapter unchanged. I see a config change in the prom scrape relabel rules from 2d ago that might have edge-case'd a label. But the immediate cause is adapter returning 5xx/timeouts.

ben (eng-sre): attaching quick logs snippet: ```2026-03-15T11:02:17Z prometheus-adapter error: upstream timeout; context deadline exceeded``` Also `kube-metrics-server` logs show `unable to fetch metrics: context deadline exceeded`.

julia (support): customers reporting increased latency and 429s at the API edge. First customer alert ~11:04. Exp of requests 2-3x normal for a few tenants but many are now being throttled.

oncall-rotation: I'm spinning up emergency reserve nodes (if autoscaler won't trigger) - requesting approval to temporarily bump instance quota for prod-gpu-a by 8 GPUs.

mike (infra): approved, do it. I'll start a manual node pool expand via the console and add a permissive taint to avoid scheduling non-inference jobs.

priya (runtime): mitigation steps I'm running in parallel: 1) restart prometheus-adapter (rolling) to restore metric path 2) increase HPA minReplicas to 20 temporarily to force scale 3) enable fallback metric (cpu-based) on inference HPA so we don't fully rely on custom metric while adapter recovers.

ben (eng-sre): doing a canary restart of prometheus-adapter now (pod prometheus-adapter-0). watching logs.

incident-bot: deploy-bot started restart of prometheus-adapter-0 (job id 789).

ben (eng-sre): prometheus-adapter-0 restarted, logs show `startup: waiting for connection to prometheus` -> recovered connection at +35s. Adapter now reporting metrics for custom/gpu_queue_depth again.

priya (runtime): HPA observed metric updates at 11:14:22 and recommended scale -> but controller respects cooldown. I applied immediate patch: `kubectl patch hpa inference -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":20}}'` to force new pods.

sara (oncall): manual scale observed, new pods provisioning, node pool expansion in progress. Queue depth is starting to trend down. API 429s reduced.

julia (support): customer alert update: We've posted to status.redwood.ai: "Investigating increased inference latency and throttling. Mitigations underway." Several customers acknowledged, one enterprise rep asked for ETA.

mike (infra): nodepool scaled +8 GPUs at 11:19, pods started scheduling to new nodes.

ben (eng-sre): monitoring shows job queue down from 820 -> 240 over 10m after pods came up. GPU utilization on new nodes ~65%. No more adapter 5xxs.

priya (runtime): root cause hypothesis: prometheus-adapter experienced transient connection saturation due to a spike in cardinality after a relabel rule change (datapoint explosion). That caused adapter to exhaust connection pool and time out upstream requests; HPA got stale metrics -> stuck. We'll open a JIRA for relabel rollback and adapter rate-limits.

sara (oncall): next steps: 1) keep HPA minReplicas at 20 for 30m and monitor 2) revert relabel rule if impact confirmed 3) bake adapter circuit-breaker for high-cardinality scrapes 4) postmortem + customer impact timeline.

julia (support): noted customer impact: ~11:04-11:22 significant throttling for 4 customers, one enterprise with bursty traf. I'll collect request ids and prepare targeted follow-up.

ben (eng-sre): adding timeline entries and logs to incident doc: https://internal.redwood/incident/4360123456 (will post full writeup).

incident-bot: incident severity updated -> P1 -> active. Pager duty rotation: oncall handoff will be at 11:45, sara will hand off to ben.

sara (oncall): handing off in 10m, ben please take postmortem ownership.

ben (eng-sre): taking postmortem ownership. I'll coordinate with runtime and infra for remediation tickets.

priya (runtime): create runbook action items: (a) relax adapter scrape window for high-cardinality targets (b) add adapter horizontal autoscaler + JVM tuning (c) implement fallback HPA metric to keep autoscaling live.

mike (infra): adding a short-term guard: throttle ingress bursts for the affected tenants (rate-limit per-customer) to reduce queue spikes while we stabilize.

sara (oncall): marking status page: "Mitigation in place, autoscaling restored, node pool expanded. Investigating root cause." Will update again at next check 11:40.

julia (support): will send a high-level email to impacted customers with timeline and mitigation notes after 11:40 check.

ben (eng-sre): metrics look stable. I'll keep watch for 30m and then schedule rollback of minReplicas.

priya (runtime): filing JIRA: INF-9721 "prometheus-adapter cardinality spike - relabel rule rollback + adapter hardening".

sara (oncall): thanks team. closing active remediation chat once we confirm no regression.

incident-bot: incident status -> monitoring.

ben (eng-sre): follow-up note: confirm whether any other clusters saw similar adapter saturation (cross-regional). I've started a cross-cluster check.

priya (runtime): cross-cluster check: cluster-b shows increased scrape latency but adapter not fully failed; will include mitigation recommendations in postmortem.

sara (oncall): handoff to ben now. ending shift.

ben (eng-sre): acknowledged handoff. continuing monitoring and will run postmortem draft.
